newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 28.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 28.

text.p: Three Mexican ports were closed on Monday to large shipping operations as a storm front hovered over the Gulf of Mexico, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1500 local/2000 GMT daily meteorological report.

Crude shipping port Dos Bocas remained shut since initially closing Sunday at 2200 local/0300 GMT, port officials said. A 500,000 barrel capacity crude tanker was reported waiting to sail from the port.
Ciudad del Carmen and Cayo Arcas were also reported shut, although port officials at Cayo Arcas said the port was operating and exporting crude as normal.
Winds at the ports were clocked at up to 45 km per hour with waves up to eleven feet high.
Gulf ports Alvarado, Nautla, Veracruz, Coatzacoalcos and Frontera were closed to small tourism and fishing boats amid winds up to 45 km/25 miles per hour.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.
Partly cloudy skies and winds up to 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per hour) with waves three to six feet high.

Weak cold front moving south-southwest and drawing clouds and light rains along the Yucatan peninsula and the coasts of Veracruz and Tabasco states. Winds up to 20 knots (38 km/22 miles) with waves three to six feet high, expected to die down later in the day.
Partly cloudy with rains and winds from 25 to 35 km per hour, winds expected to relax by Tuesday morning.
